content: The data center hummed like a cathedral of the damned, its aisles of servers glowing like cryptic tombstones under the sickly flicker of emergency lights. Neon blue strips cast long shadows where the dust hadn’t settled in years, and the air tasted of ozone and bad decisions. Jack Veil, ex-hacker turned security merc, leaned against a rack of blades, his trench coat soaked through from the rain outside. A cigarette dangled from his lips—against regs, but the skeleton crew was too busy watching the ceiling leak to care. His tablet buzzed: a redacted error log, a dead sysadmin’s last message blinking in Morse code through a malfunctioning LED. *"They’re in the backbone,"* it read. *"Run."* But Veil didn’t run. He’d come to bury ghosts, not join ’em. Somewhere, a cooling fan whined like a dying animal. On the security feed, a flicker—a woman in a red-scarved avatar, her pixels smiling from the depths of the dark web. His contact. His mark. His reckoning. The servers thrummed louder. The floor vibrated. Data was dying. And Veil knew, in that cold sweat of ones and zeros, the whole place was a coffin waiting to seal.
